The **Process** standard library runs external commands. `Run Process` returns
a result object with `.rc` (exit code), `.stdout`, and `.stderr`. This part's
workspace ships a small CLI, `tools/inventory.py`, to drive.

## Task 1 — Run the inventory CLI and read its output

**Goal:** create `checks/process.robot` that imports `Process`, runs
`tools/inventory.py list`, asserts a clean exit, and checks a product name in
its output.

Here is the same pattern over a different command. Adapt it to the CLI.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    Process

*** Test Cases ***
Python Reports Its Version
    ${result}=    Run Process    python3    --version
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${result.rc}    0
    Should Contain    ${result.stdout}    Python
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the suite imports `Process` and uses `Run Process`.

<!-- hint -->
Run the CLI by passing its path and subcommand as separate cells:
`Run Process    python3    tools/inventory.py    list`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
A clean run exits `0` — assert `Should Be Equal As Integers    ${result.rc}    0`
— and `list` prints product names, so `Should Contain    ${result.stdout}    Trail Backpack`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    Process

*** Test Cases ***
List Products With The CLI
    ${result}=    Run Process    python3    tools/inventory.py    list
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${result.rc}    0
    Should Contain    ${result.stdout}    Trail Backpack
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it green

Run:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the CLI runs, exits 0, and its output lists the products.
